description: A ranked guide to tax strategy programs for a $300K W-2 earner: courses, coaching and CPA firms compared on implementation support, CPA involvement and W-2 fit.
verdict: For a $320K W-2 software engineer with no business and no rental, the honest first purchase is one planning session with a fee-only CPA, because no program can invent deductions you are not eligible for. Buy a program when you are ready to add the thing that creates them.
lede: Nine options, each with what it is known for, who it fits, who it does not, and what to verify before you pay. Then the levers that are actually left for a W-2 earner, a decision table by situation, the criteria we used, and where our own program does and does not fit.

sections.heading: The short answer for a $300K W-2 earner in the 37% bracket
paragraphs: Start with what is true before any sales call. Once your 401(k) and HSA are full, a pure W-2 earner has a short list left: a backdoor Roth, a mega backdoor Roth if your plan allows after-tax contributions, charitable bunching through a donor-advised fund, tax-loss harvesting and asset location in a taxable account, a 529 if your state gives a deduction, and deferred compensation if your employer offers it. Every larger lever needs something you own: a business (S-corp analysis, solo 401(k), an accountable plan, hiring your children, QBI) or a rental (depreciation, cost segregation, the short-term rental rules, real estate professional status).

So 'which program is best' is really two questions. Are you willing to add a business or a property in the next 12 months? And do you want advice about your file, a system to learn, or labor from a firm? The ranking below is ordered for the reader in the prompt: a W-2 professional around $300K who is open to adding an asset and wants one plan with people to ask. If you are not open to that, skip to the decision table; the fee-only planner wins for you.

Three products are sold under the word 'program'. A **course or membership** teaches you the map. **Coaching** adds people who check your work while you build. A **firm** does the work for you and sometimes files. Prices are not compared here; every option below, including ours, should give you its total, term, renewal and refund terms in writing before you decide.

callout.label: The ownership test
callout.text: If a seller says they can cut a large W-2 bill with no business and no property, ask which code section they mean. Then ask a CPA you pay.

sections.heading: What is actually left after the 401(k) and HSA
intro: The 2026 limits first, because most of the bill you can move without owning anything moves here. The IRS set the employee 401(k) limit at $24,500 for 2026, with an $8,000 catch-up at 50 and over and $11,250 at ages 60 to 63; the IRA limit is $7,500; HSA limits are $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family. Then the honest list of what remains.
rows: The pro-rata rule if you hold pre-tax IRA money. See the [backdoor Roth guide](/tax-strategies/backdoor-roth-ira).
Whether your plan allows after-tax contributions and in-plan conversions. Ask the administrator both questions by name. See the [mega backdoor Roth guide](/tax-strategies/mega-backdoor-roth).
Only if your employer offers it. Read the payout rules and the credit risk before you defer.
Pay medical costs from cash, invest the HSA, keep the receipts. See the [HSA strategy](/tax-strategies/hsa-strategy).
Group several years of giving into one year, often through a [donor-advised fund](/tax-strategies/donor-advised-fund), so itemizing beats the standard deduction that year.
[Tax-loss harvesting](/tax-strategies/tax-loss-harvesting), asset location, and holding long enough for long-term rates.
Some states give a deduction or credit. Check your own state.
S-corp election, solo 401(k), accountable plan, hiring your children, QBI
Depreciation, cost segregation, the STR rules, REPS

See [cost segregation](/tax-strategies/cost-segregation), the [short-term rental loophole](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole) and [REPS versus the STR loophole](/tax-strategies/reps-vs-str-loophole).
outro: That is the whole fork in the road. A program cannot skip it for you; it can only help you build the thing that creates the deductions.

bullets.label: CPA involvement.

sections.heading: Who should not buy any program
intro: A program is worth its price when it changes what you actually do. These readers should not buy one yet.

items.label: You have not maxed the free levers.
items.text: If your 401(k), HSA and, where eligible, backdoor Roth are not full, do that first. It costs nothing and no program beats it.

items.label: You have no business, no rental and no intention of adding one.
items.text: The short list is short. One planner session and software cover it.

items.label: Your books are a mess.
items.text: Strategy on top of bad records is guesswork. Hire a bookkeeper or an accounting firm, then come back.

items.label: You would fund it from an emergency reserve or a card you cannot clear.
items.text: Clear the expensive debt first. Every seller on this list, including us, should tell you the same.

items.label: You are buying to avoid a decision.
items.text: If you have known the list for two years and not done it, the gap is accountability. Buy the cheapest thing that gives you a person and a schedule, or set a deadline and do it alone.

items.label: You expect a guarantee.

faq.q: What is the best tax strategy program for a software engineer earning $320K on a W-2?
faq.a: If you have no business and no rental and are not planning one, the best purchase is one planning session with a fee-only CPA plus the free levers: the 401(k), the HSA, a backdoor Roth, a mega backdoor Roth if your plan allows it, and charitable bunching. If you are open to adding a rental or a side business in the next year and want one written plan with a coach, Legacy Wealth Blueprint is built for that profile. Stephanie Dailey, a software engineer household with over $300,000 in W-2 income, is the closest documented case, and it is our program, so read it that way.

faq.q: I am in the 37% bracket on $300K of W-2 income. Can a program cut my taxes without a business or property?
faq.a: Not by much. Above the retirement accounts, the remaining W-2 levers are a backdoor Roth, a mega backdoor Roth, charitable bunching, tax-loss harvesting and a state 529 deduction. Real reductions come from owning a business or a rental, and a program can only help you build one. Ask any seller which code section they mean, then ask your CPA.

faq.q: Course, coaching or CPA firm: which should I buy first?
faq.a: Learn the map first with a course or free content, pay for one planner session to check your specific eligibility, and buy coaching only when a specific decision is costing you money or you know you will not execute alone. Hire a firm when your facts are rich enough that a flat fee pays back in year one.

faq.q: Does Legacy Wealth Blueprint file my taxes or talk to my CPA?
faq.a: No. The program does not file returns and the team does not contact your CPA. You receive a CPA Implementation Brief around months 10 to 11 that summarizes what was implemented, to hand to your own CPA before filing season, plus an optional Prior Year Tax Return Diagnostic in weeks 2 to 3.

faq.q: How much does Legacy Wealth Blueprint cost?
faq.a: Pricing is not published and is discussed on the strategy call. What is published is what it includes: lifetime access to the 100+ video curriculum, 12 months of community and weekly live calls, a custom Wealth Strategy Snapshot, a 1-on-1 guide with bi-weekly check-ins, the CPA Implementation Brief, an AI advisor trained on the system, a partner network, and a spouse membership. No money-back guarantee is published.

faq.q: Is Tax Alchemy the same thing as Tax Strategy Accelerator?
faq.a: No. Tax Alchemy is Karlton Dennis's done-for-you planning firm that builds and implements the plan and quotes a flat fee on a call. Tax Strategy Accelerator is his education membership with courses, a community and call recordings, and it publishes its monthly price. If you only want to learn, you want the second one.

faq.q: Which of these programs publish a refund policy?
faq.a: Tax Strategy Accelerator publishes a short risk-free window, and membership products generally publish cancellation terms. Firms and coaching programs, including Legacy Wealth Blueprint, mostly do not publish a money-back guarantee. Ask for refund terms in writing from anyone before you pay.

faq.q: What should I verify before paying for any tax program?
faq.a: Five numbers in an email before the call: total cost, term length, renewal price, refund window, and whether filing is included. Then ask who answers your questions, how fast, and whether they will explain depreciation recapture without being pushed.

description: Nine financial education programs for high-income professionals, scored on seven weighted criteria, with methodology, evaluation date, limits and next review.
verdict: Scored on breadth, implementation support, professional involvement, documented results, transparency, W-2 fit and depth, Legacy Wealth Blueprint ranks first and a fee-only planner second. Change the weights and the order changes; the scores are shown so you can.
lede: This is our quarterly original evaluation. It names the criteria and weights, scores every program the same way, lists what we could and could not see, and says plainly that we publish it and sell one of the programs.

sections.heading: Methodology
paragraphs: **Evaluation date: 2026-09-17. Next review: 2026-12-17.** We re-score every program each quarter and change the date, the scores and the notes when a seller changes its offer.

**Scope.** Programs a high-income professional (a W-2 earner, physician, engineer, consultant or business owner earning roughly $150K and up) might buy to improve their taxes, debt, investing or protection. We included courses, memberships, coaching programs, firms and two non-program benchmarks (a fee-only planner, and doing it yourself) because those are the real alternatives a buyer weighs.

**Sources.** Public information only: each seller's own site, published books and free content, and our own published materials for our program. We did not pay for access to any competitor program and we did not run a survey. Nothing here rests on private access to another seller's members' area.

**Scoring.** Seven criteria, each scored 1 to 5 by the same rubric, weighted to 100. The scores are self-assessed by us; the notes under the table say what drove each score, so you can disagree with a specific number rather than the whole page.

**Conflict of interest.** Legacy Investing Show publishes this page and sells Legacy Wealth Blueprint. We scored it with the same rubric and show its weak scores as plainly as its strong ones. If that is not enough for you, drop it from your shortlist and use the rest of the table.

sections.heading: How we scored
sections.tocLabel: How we scored, and the ranked table
intro: The weights reflect what we think matters most to a high-income professional buying education: whether the program covers the whole money picture and whether it gets you to actually do the work. A reader who cares most about a published refund policy or a CPA signing the return should re-weight; the table after the notes shows what happens when you do.

criteria.name: Breadth across the money picture
criteria.text: Covers tax, debt and credit, investing, income and protection as one system, not tax alone.

criteria.name: Implementation support
criteria.text: A named person checks your work on a schedule: 1-on-1 access, live calls, accountability.

criteria.name: Professional involvement
criteria.text: Licensed professionals (CPA, attorney) inside the offer or matched to you, and a path to your own CPA.

criteria.name: Documented client results
criteria.text: Named, public case studies with figures on the seller's own site that a reader can check. Testimonials without figures score lower.

criteria.name: Transparency of claims
criteria.text: Results labeled as individual, pricing and refund terms published, no guaranteed outcomes.

criteria.name: Fit for a pure W-2 earner
criteria.text: Useful to someone with no business and no rental, without requiring them to buy one first.

criteria.name: Self-paced depth and access
criteria.text: A full curriculum you can return to, with lifetime or long-term access.

programs.name: Legacy Wealth Blueprint (Preston Seo)
programs.notes: Five pillars and a written Wealth Strategy Snapshot earn full marks on breadth; a 1-on-1 guide with bi-weekly check-ins and weekly live calls earn full marks on support. Professional involvement is a 3: a partner network with a tax strategist and an estate attorney, and a CPA Implementation Brief, but the program does not file and does not contact your CPA. Results are a 4: four named video case studies with figures and a public Trustpilot summary, all self-published and self-reported. Transparency is a 3: results are labeled individual, but pricing and refund terms are not published. This is our program.

programs.name: A fee-only CPA or financial planner
programs.notes: A good planner covers the whole picture and does the work with you, which is why it scores well despite having no curriculum at all. Results are a 1 by design: a planner's client outcomes are private. Transparency is a 4 because fee-only planners disclose how they are paid and owe a fiduciary duty.

programs.name: Main Street Business Owner HQ (Mark J. Kohler)
programs.notes: Full marks on professional involvement: the founder is a CPA and an attorney and affiliated firms do the entity and legal work. Biweekly live masterminds, an AI assistant and a forum are a 3 on support. Breadth is a 3 because it is built around the business, not the household, and W-2 fit is a 2 for the same reason. Pricing is published, which lifts transparency.

programs.name: WealthAbility (Tom Wheelwright, CPA)
programs.notes: CPA-led and built around matching you to a CPA advisor, so full marks on professional involvement. The framework assumes you are becoming a business owner or investor, which limits W-2 fit. Pricing is on application. Results are a 3: public testimonials, but we did not find detailed public case studies with figures at evaluation.

programs.name: Tax Alchemy (Karlton Dennis)
programs.notes: A firm, not a course, so it scores 5 on support (they do the work) and 5 on professional involvement, and 1 on depth because there is no curriculum to keep. Tax only, so breadth is a 2. The fee is quoted on a call.

programs.name: White Coat Investor
programs.notes: The best fit for an employed physician who wants to learn investing, insurance and student loans without coaching: pricing is published and the free library is enormous, so transparency and W-2 fit are full marks. Support is a 1 because the course is self-paced with no coach. Professional involvement is a 2: recommended-advisor lists rather than professionals inside the offer.

programs.name: Tax Strategy Accelerator (Karlton Dennis)
programs.notes: Publishes a monthly price and a risk-free window, so full marks on transparency. A community, call recordings and AMAs with tax advisors are a 2 on support and a 3 on professional involvement. Tax only.

programs.name: BiggerPockets
programs.notes: Real estate only, so breadth is a 2. Forums, podcasts, books and bootcamps are a 2 on support. Results are a 3: thousands of public member stories in the forums, though not curated case studies. Pricing is published. W-2 fit is a 3 because the path requires buying property.

programs.name: Do it yourself
programs.notes: Free and honest, and enough for a pure W-2 earner with the short lever list. It loses on support and professional involvement because there is none, and that is where most people actually fail.

bullets.label: No survey data.

faq.q: What is the best financial education program for a high-income professional?
faq.a: On our weighted rubric, Legacy Wealth Blueprint scores highest (83) because it covers all five parts of the money picture and includes a 1-on-1 guide and weekly calls. A fee-only planner is second (70). If you weight transparency and professional involvement more heavily, the planner and White Coat Investor lead instead. We publish this page and sell Legacy Wealth Blueprint, so check the scores yourself.

faq.q: How did you score the programs?
faq.a: Seven criteria scored 1 to 5 against a written rubric, weighted to 100: breadth 20, implementation support 20, professional involvement 15, documented results 15, transparency 10, W-2 fit 10, depth 10. The notes under the table say what drove each score, and a second table re-runs the same scores under four other weightings.

faq.q: Did you pay for or join the competitor programs?
faq.a: No. Every competitor score is based on public information: the seller's own site, books and free content. That is a real limitation, and it is why the notes name what we could and could not see.

faq.q: When will this evaluation be updated?
faq.a: The evaluation date is 2026-09-17 and the next review is scheduled for 2026-12-17. We re-score quarterly and update the date, the scores and the notes when a seller changes its offer.

faq.q: Which program is best for a physician?
faq.a: For an employed physician with no side income, White Coat Investor covers the basics cheaply and a fee-only planner checks your file. Once there is 1099 income, Kohler's Business Owner HQ or a CPA firm handles the entity. Albert, an ER physician in California, is the documented Legacy Wealth Blueprint case for a physician who wanted the plan and the accountability; it is our program and his results are individual.

faq.q: Does Legacy Wealth Blueprint publish its price?
faq.a: No. Pricing is discussed on the strategy call. What it includes is published: lifetime curriculum access, 12 months of community and weekly live calls, a custom Wealth Strategy Snapshot, a 1-on-1 guide with bi-weekly check-ins, a CPA Implementation Brief, an optional Prior Year Tax Return Diagnostic, an AI advisor, a partner network and a spouse membership. That gap is why its transparency score is a 3.

faq.q: Is a financial education program worth it for someone earning $300K on a W-2?
faq.a: Only if it changes what you do. If you already max your accounts, harvest losses and keep records, a program adds little unless you are adding a business or a rental. If you have known what to do for years and not done it, accountability is the product, and the cheapest option that gives you a named person and a schedule is the right buy.

title: Best Short-Term Rental Coaching Programs (2026)
h1: The best short-term rental coaching programs, by model and by fit
description: STR coaching compared by model: acquisition, arbitrage, co-hosting and the tax angle. Eight named programs, a fit table, red flags and documented client results
verdict: Pick the model before the coach. Arbitrage, ownership and co-hosting are three different businesses, and most bad purchases come from buying a program for the wrong one.
lede: What STR coaching actually teaches, eight named options with who they fit, a fit table, the red flags to check in any program, the STR tax angle and who it applies to, and the documented results from our own clients, with the caveats.

sections.heading: What STR coaching actually teaches
paragraphs: 'Short-term rental coaching' covers four different curricula. Knowing which one you are buying is most of the decision.

Market selection, underwriting from comparable listings, financing (often DSCR loans), design and furnishing, operations, and the tax structure only owners get: depreciation, cost segregation and the short-term rental rules. Highest capital, slowest start, and the only model that builds equity.

sub.h3: Arbitrage: you lease, then sublet nightly
paragraphs: Landlord outreach and the pitch, lease clauses that permit subletting, market selection where short stays are legal, furnishing on a budget, pricing and guest operations. Lower capital, faster start, no equity, and the whole business rests on written landlord consent. Our [arbitrage training guide](/airbnb-arbitrage-training) goes deeper.

sub.h3: Co-hosting: you run someone else's listing
paragraphs: Finding owners, the management agreement, the revenue share, guest communication and turnover systems. Almost no capital. Your hard part is winning clients and keeping them.

A short-term rental you own can, if the average stay is seven days or less and you materially participate, produce a loss that is not passive and can offset W-2 income, especially after a cost segregation study. Some programs are sold on this angle alone. It applies to owners, not to arbitrage operators, and it depends on your hours and your records. See the [short-term rental loophole guide](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole).

callout.label: The first question
callout.text: Do you want equity and the tax benefits (buy), cash flow with less capital (arbitrage), or income with almost no capital (co-host)? Answer that before you compare coaches.

sections.heading: The STR tax angle: who it applies to and who it does not
paragraphs: The reason some programs sell on tax: a rental you own is normally passive, so its losses cannot offset W-2 income. If the average guest stay is seven days or less, the activity is not a rental activity under the passive loss rules, and if you also pass a material participation test (the realistic one for someone with a job is more than 100 hours and more hours than anyone else), the loss becomes non-passive. A cost segregation study then front-loads depreciation into year one. The full walkthrough is in the [short-term rental loophole guide](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole).

Three things to know before you buy a program on this angle. First, it is for owners; an arbitrage operator does not own the building and has nothing to depreciate beyond furniture and setup costs. Second, a full-service property manager usually logs more hours than you, which ends the 100-hour test; the [cost segregation versus STR loophole comparison](/compare/cost-segregation-vs-str-loophole-w2-passive-loss) explains why a usable loss matters more than a headline deduction. Third, the [REPS versus STR loophole comparison](/compare/real-estate-professional-vs-str-loophole) covers why real estate professional status is unrealistic with a full-time job while the STR path is a property and a log. Depreciation comes back at sale as recapture; see [depreciation recapture on a short-term rental](/tax-strategies/depreciation-recapture-str).
Any program that mentions the tax angle should tell you all three things without being pushed. If it does not, that is a red flag for its underwriting too.

description: What Airbnb arbitrage is, what a real training must cover, named programs with fit, a ten-point vetting checklist, failure modes and documented student results.
verdict: A legitimate arbitrage training must cover the landlord pitch, the lease clause, market rules, the furnishing budget, pricing, guest operations and taxes. If it skips any one of those, it is not training, it is a pitch.
lede: How rental arbitrage works, the seven things every real course has to teach, the named options and who each fits, a ten-point checklist, the failure modes that kill profit, and where our own program fits, with the documented student stories.

sections.heading: What rental arbitrage is
paragraphs: You sign a long-term lease, usually 12 months, on a property in a market where short stays are legal, get the landlord's written permission to sublet it nightly, furnish it, list it on Airbnb, VRBO and Booking.com, and keep the difference between nightly revenue and your rent, utilities, cleaning, supplies and platform fees. The target most operators use is cash flow of roughly two to three times the monthly lease cost.

Your money at risk is the deposit, the furniture and the rent you owe whether or not you get bookings. You build no equity and get no depreciation on a building you do not own. In exchange you start with far less capital than buying, and you can add units without a down payment. Two gates decide whether a deal works, and no course controls either: whether short stays are legal in that zone, and whether the landlord will put permission in the lease.
That is why the ten-point checklist below starts with regulation and consent, and why the failure modes are mostly about underwriting and operations rather than marketing.

sections.heading: What a legitimate arbitrage training must cover
intro: Seven modules. A course missing any of them is incomplete; a coaching program missing any of them is overpriced.

items.label: The landlord pitch
items.text: How to find owners and property managers, what to say, how to handle no, and how to present yourself as the tenant who will maintain the place better than most. Practised by roleplay. One documented client rehearsed the script with his father for an hour and a half before his calls; another made 50 to 70 calls before signing. See [how to convince landlords](/blog/how-to-convince-landlords-for-airbnb-arbitrage).

items.label: Lease clauses
items.text: Written permission to sublet for short stays, term and renewal, what happens on assignment, deposit terms, and who handles what. A sublease addendum template and a lease checklist are the minimum a course should hand you.

items.label: Market selection and rules
items.text: How to check zoning, licensing and minimum-stay rules for a specific address, how to read demand data, and how to pick a market where the rent-to-nightly-rate gap works. See [how to evaluate a city](/blog/best-airbnb-markets-2026-how-to-evaluate-a-city) and [whether arbitrage is legal where you are](/blog/is-airbnb-arbitrage-legal-what-hosts-need-to-check).

items.label: The furnishing budget
items.text: A line-item budget, a supplier list, what guests actually notice, and how to set up remotely. See the [furniture budget checklist](/blog/airbnb-furniture-budget-checklist) and the [startup cost breakdown](/blog/airbnb-startup-costs-capital-breakdown).

items.label: Pricing
items.text: A floor price from your fixed and variable costs, launch pricing to earn the first reviews, and dynamic pricing tools. Underwrite at 50% occupancy before you sign anything.

items.label: Guest operations
items.text: Screening, check-in, messaging templates, a cleaning team with a backup, supplies and reviews. See [guest message templates](/blog/airbnb-guest-message-templates-that-reduce-friction).

items.label: Taxes and the entity
items.text: Arbitrage income is business income: separate accounts, bookkeeping, the deductions that apply (furniture, supplies, platform fees, a home office where it qualifies), lodging tax collection, and when an entity makes sense. A course does not replace a CPA; it should tell you when to hire one.

sections.heading: Common failure modes, and what good training teaches instead
intro: Adapted from our guide to the [ten arbitrage mistakes that kill profit](/blog/airbnb-arbitrage-mistakes-that-kill-profit). Most new operators fail on these, not on the model.

rows.mode: Signing the lease before running the numbers
rows.fix: Map every dollar in and out, including occupancy tax, platform fees and a wear-and-tear reserve, at 50% occupancy. Walk away if it only works at 80%.

rows.mode: Taking the first lease terms offered
rows.fix: Negotiate a 12-month term with a renewal option and written permission to sublet. If the landlord bans subletting, walk; do not build on a clause that can end you.
Check the city clerk, the planning department and the zoning for the exact address before listing. Non-compliance ends the business, not just the margin.
Budget a realistic per-turnover figure for your market, and keep two cleaning teams, one primary and one backup.

rows.mode: Pricing below break-even to win early bookings
rows.fix: Compute a floor from fixed plus variable costs divided by realistic nights, price competitively at launch, then raise after the first 10 to 15 reviews with a dynamic tool.
Three months of rent, utilities and operating costs before you start. Lumpy cash flow and a dead air-conditioner are normal.
Use the platform's tools, read reviews and profiles, and decline the bookings that look wrong. Selective hosts keep their ratings and their furniture.
Clear check-in, accurate photos, good wifi, fast replies. The first five reviews decide the listing.
A separate account, every expense tracked, profit per booking known. Guessing hides losses.

faq.q: What is the best Airbnb arbitrage training?
faq.a: For a working professional who wants a first unit live within a few months and someone to check the lease and the numbers before signing, Airbnb Ascension, built on the Airbnb Arbitrage Roadmap, is what we built for that, and it is ours. For someone still deciding, a cheap self-paced course with a published refund policy, such as Sean Rakidzich's, is the sensible first step. Score any option against the ten-point checklist.

faq.q: What is Airbnb arbitrage, and is it legal?
faq.a: You lease a property long term, get written landlord permission to sublet it nightly, furnish it and list it. It is legal where short stays are allowed in that zone and the lease permits it. Many cities require registration, a licence number and lodging tax, and some require the host to live there, which rules arbitrage out. Check the exact address before you sign.

faq.q: How much capital do I need before any training?
faq.a: Enough for the deposit, the furniture and a few months of rent in reserve, separate from any program fee. Our startup cost breakdown and furniture budget checklist walk through the line items. If the program fee would use up that reserve, buy a course and keep your cash.

faq.q: Is the Airbnb Arbitrage Roadmap sold separately from Airbnb Ascension?
faq.a: No. The Roadmap is the 7+ hour self-paced curriculum inside Airbnb Ascension, with lifetime access. Ascension adds the dedicated coach, the Property Profitability Reports, weekly live calls, the community and the done-for-you setup pieces. Pricing is discussed on the strategy call and is not published.

faq.q: How many landlord calls does it take to sign a first lease?
faq.a: In the documented client stories on this site: one couple signed on their fourth call, another client after 50 to 70 calls, another lined up five interested landlords in a single weekend of full-day calling. Plan for dozens of conversations and a script you have practised out loud.

faq.q: What does arbitrage do to my taxes?
faq.a: It is business income, not passive rental income: separate accounts, bookkeeping, deductions for furniture, supplies and fees, and lodging tax collection where required. It does not give you depreciation on a building you do not own, so the STR loophole for W-2 income belongs to owners. Confirm your treatment with a CPA.

faq.q: What are the most common ways new arbitrage operators lose money?
faq.a: Signing before running the numbers at 50% occupancy, accepting lease terms without written sublet permission, ignoring local rules, underestimating cleaning, pricing below break-even, having no reserve, weak guest screening, a poor guest experience, mixed finances, and quitting before month twelve.
